summary: The candidate is a partial fix. It corrects the issue's 42-token capture geometry from eight unequal rows to seven equal width-six rows and fixes the independently reproduced overlapping-storage failure in DSV4 raw metadata replay. However, independent boundary testing shows that 41, 43, and 47 tokens still produce unequal request rows. An equal-block-only EngramHasher would still reject those compact-ragged layouts. This checkout and candidate contain no Engram implementation, so per-request hash context and numerical hash output could not be validated. The full DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash capture and first-forward path is also unavailable on the assigned single AMD GPU.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-11e00af9083e/venv/bin/python -c 'exercise build_capture_verify_lens at the recorded base for 6,12,24,41,42,43,47,48 tokens using the actual base slot selection'
tests.what_was_measured: At the exact recorded base, 42 tokens and eight slots produced [6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5], reproducing the original capture assertion geometry. Other nonuniform boundaries were also recorded.
Both DSV4RawVerifyMetadata.copy_ and DSV4RawDecodeMetadata.copy_ raised PyTorch's overlapping-memory RuntimeError on the assigned MI350X, reproducing the later failure mechanism.
Candidate regression suite: 14 tests passed with 8 subtests. Imports resolved to candidate Python sources under /job/repo.
Both candidate metadata-copy paths passed with overlapping real-device tensor views on AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950).

tests.what_was_measured: Packing invariants and error handling passed, and 42 became seven equal rows. But 41 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,5], 43 -> [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5], and 47 -> [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5], preserving the reviewed Engram counterexamples.

gpu_evidence: PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 executed overlapping-view copy cases on AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950. The base failed and the candidate passed.
remaining_counterexamples: At width 6, 41 tokens use seven rows [6,6,6,6,6,6,5], which is incompatible with the issue-described equal-block Engram target-verify assertion.
At width 6, 43 tokens use eight rows [6,6,6,5,5,5,5,5], which is incompatible with the issue-described equal-block Engram target-verify assertion.
At width 6, 47 tokens use eight rows [6,6,6,6,6,6,6,5], which is incompatible with the issue-described equal-block Engram target-verify assertion.
No EngramHasher or engram.py exists in the prepared base or exact candidate, so per-request hash context and numerical hash outputs cannot be compared with an independent reference.
The full first-forward path after capture was not run with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; only the isolated real-device DSV4 overlapping-metadata mechanism was reproduced and verified.
remaining_limitations: The assigned architecture is one AMD Instinct MI350X (ROCm 7.2), not the reported four-node NVIDIA GB10 CUDA 13 TP4/EP4 deployment.
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights and an Engram implementation are absent, preventing full model capture, serving, hashing, and semantic validation.
No C++, FlyDSL, LLVM, or other native source changed in the candidate, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify Engram, DeepSeek-V4.1, DSV4 attention semantics, or a distributed TP4/EP4 workload and was therefore not used as substitute proof.
